entries.clue: Unable to fly in cloud (6)

indicatorNotes.to fly: letters sent flying are scattered and rearranged

annotation.surface: A grounded bird, or aircraft, stuck in cloud.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Unable to fly' reads as one phrase meaning flightless, so you look for a word like that; split it and 'unable' is the fodder, 'to fly' the instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: A nebula is a cloud of gas and dust in space.

entries.clue: Broadcaster snorting cocaine – a means of getting high (5,3)

indicatorNotes.snorting: the broadcaster takes the drug up inside itself

blocks.note: a cabler is a cable-television broadcaster

annotation.surface: A scandal story about a media figure caught with cocaine.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Getting high' completes the drugs picture, but the definition means altitude: a cable car carries you up a mountain.
annotation.definitionFit: A cable car hauls passengers up steep slopes on an overhead cable.

entries.clue: User of special make-up (6)

blocks.note: toner is a cosmetic applied to the skin

annotation.surface: Someone who wears unusual cosmetics.
annotation.walkthrough: 'User' looks like a plain noun for anyone who uses something; here it is the drug user, and a stoner is a habitual cannabis smoker.
annotation.definitionFit: A stoner is someone who regularly uses cannabis, a drug user.

entries.clue: Hides recipes in Paul’s cryptic (7)

indicatorNotes.cryptic: the letters are hidden in a puzzling order

blocks.note: R = recipe (as on a prescription), so two of them

annotation.surface: Paul, a setter's name, has tucked some recipes away in his crossword.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hides' is a verb meaning thrashes, not conceals: to hide someone is to beat them. Paul is also a Guardian setter, which makes the surface a wink.
annotation.definitionFit: To larrup is to thrash, as is to hide (tan someone's hide).

entries.clue: Spot of Jazz perhaps led by Duke (6)

indicatorNotes.led by: the Duke's letter goes in front

blocks.note: Jazz is a variety of apple; 'perhaps' flags an example

annotation.surface: Duke Ellington leading a band in a spot of jazz.
annotation.walkthrough: Jazz next to Duke summons Ellington, but Jazz here is an apple variety, and the capital J is there to mislead.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, both as verb and noun: a dapple is one of the round patches on a dappled horse.

entries.clue: Solitary Shakespearian lover dumping a jerk (8)

indicatorNotes.dumping: the lover throws out the letter A

blocks.note: HERMIA, a lover in A Midsummer Night's Dream, loses her A
a tic is an involuntary jerk

annotation.surface: A lonely Shakespeare character who has ditched a creep.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Jerk' invites the insult, the lout being dumped; it is really a twitch. HERMIA is one of the four lovers lost in the wood in A Midsummer Night's Dream.
annotation.definitionFit: Hermitic means like a hermit: solitary.

entries.clue: Saint-Saëns a bit lively (9)

indicatorNotes.lively: the letters are stirred into motion

annotation.surface: A music critic finds a Saint-Saëns piece fairly lively.
annotation.walkthrough: The hyphen welds 'Saint' to 'Saëns' so you read one composer's name; break it and 'Saint' is the definition, with the rest scrambled.
annotation.definitionFit: Saint Sebastian is the martyr traditionally shown shot with arrows.

entries.clue: Looked at coffee on the counter (5)

indicatorNotes.on the counter: counter as in running counter to, going the opposite way

annotation.surface: Eyeing a cup of coffee sitting on a café counter.
annotation.walkthrough: 'On the counter' is where a café serves your coffee; read counter as contrary and it turns DECAF around.
annotation.definitionFit: To face something is to look towards it.

entries.clue: Name ships after people from city (9)

indicatorNotes.after: the ships come after the name

annotation.surface: An instruction to name ships after a city's inhabitants.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Name ships after' reads as christening vessels in someone's honour; 'after' is really positional, and 'Name' is a verb meaning to confer a title, as when a knight is dubbed.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain demonym: the city is Dublin, and James Joyce's story collection takes the word as its title.

entries.clue: In the mirror, Big Bird starts to prepare shaving foam (5)

indicatorNotes.In the mirror: a mirror shows things back to front
indicatorNotes.starts to: take the first letters of the following words

blocks.note: the emu is a very large flightless bird
first letters of Prepare and Shaving
reversal indicator: a mirror image runs back to front

annotation.surface: Big Bird from Sesame Street getting ready for a shave at the mirror.
annotation.walkthrough: Capitalised, Big Bird is the Sesame Street character; it just means a large bird. 'Shaving foam' looks like one phrase, but 'foam' alone is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Spume is foam or froth, especially on waves.

entries.clue: Is that Hazel O’Connor finally wearing shirt? (4)

annotation.definitionNote: a definition by example, posed as a question

indicatorNotes.finally: 'finally' means at the end, so only the closing letter of O'Connor is used
indicatorNotes.wearing: a body wearing a shirt is inside it, so the letter goes inside the shirt

annotation.surface: Is that the singer Hazel O'Connor on stage in a shirt?
annotation.walkthrough: Hazel O'Connor is a British singer, so the name reads as one person; split them and hazel is a tree. The question mark flags that hazel is only one example of a tree.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example turned into a question: hazel is one kind of the thing being asked about.

entries.clue: May Queen overtaking close to traffic sign (6)

indicatorNotes.overtaking: CAN and ER take the C over, wrapping round it
indicatorNotes.close to: the last letter of the next word

blocks.note: may = can, as in giving permission

annotation.surface: The May Queen of a village fete zooming past near a road sign.
annotation.walkthrough: 'May Queen' is a single English tradition, a girl crowned at a spring festival; separate the words and May is the verb can. 'Traffic sign' also splits, leaving 'sign' as the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: 'sign' is short for star sign, and the crab is the fourth of the twelve.

entries.clue: Go through in style introducing wingers for extra time (8)

indicatorNotes.introducing: the style comes first and leads in what follows
indicatorNotes.wingers for: wingers play on the edges, so take each word's outer letters

annotation.surface: A football manager bringing on wide players to get through extra time.
annotation.walkthrough: Wingers and extra time belong to football; a winger works the edge of the pitch, so here the wingers are each word's outer letters.
annotation.definitionFit: To permeate is to pass or spread through something.

entries.clue: Strip clubs having forked out for protection (7)

indicatorNotes.out: FORKED is knocked out of shape
indicatorNotes.for protection: the rearranged letters wrap round and protect C

annotation.surface: Clubs have paid out for security.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Forked out' is a phrase for paying up, and 'protection' suggests a racket; 'Strip' is the definition in the sense of removing a priest's office.
annotation.definitionFit: A specialised synonym: the frock is the cleric's robe, so removing it strips him of his office.

entries.clue: Descriptive words lit up Pete Seeger’s first hit (8)

indicatorNotes.lit up: lit means drunk, so the letters reel about
indicatorNotes.first: take the first letter of Seeger

annotation.surface: Adjectives light up the folk singer Pete Seeger's first hit record.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lit up' reads as illuminated praise; take lit as drunk and the letters stagger. 'Hit' looks like the record but is fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: Epithets are descriptive words or phrases attached to a name.

entries.clue: Sea creature caught by Scotsman (4)

indicatorNotes.by: next to: C sits beside RAB

blocks.note: Rab is a typical Scottish name

annotation.surface: A fisherman from Scotland landing something from the sea.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Caught by' is one phrase on the surface; split it and 'caught' is C and 'by' simply places it next to RAB.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: the crustacean with pincers is one of many animals living in the sea.

entries.clue: Home counties member eating a fish (7)

blocks.note: the Home Counties lie round London in the South East
member = penis, for which cock is slang

annotation.surface: A member of a suburban club near London tucking into fish.
annotation.walkthrough: The Home Counties are the counties around London, abbreviated SE for South East. 'Member' reads as a club member; it is the cruder sense.
annotation.definitionFit: Sea cock is an old name for the gurnard, a fish.

entries.clue: Cry of derision about hospital blanket (5-3)

indicatorNotes.about: 'about' in its sense of around, so the cry is placed around the H

blocks.note: a catcall is a jeering whistle or shout
H = hospital, as on road signs

annotation.surface: Jeering at a hospital's bedding.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hospital blanket' reads as bedding; 'blanket' is really the adjective, as in a blanket ban.
annotation.definitionFit: A catch-all rule, like a blanket one, covers everything.

entries.clue: Painter left snail-like tracks (1,1,5)

blocks.note: RY = railway, which runs on tracks

annotation.surface: An artist leaving a trail like a snail's.
annotation.walkthrough: L. S. Lowry painted crowded northern English industrial scenes with matchstick people. 'Left' reads as departed; it is just the letter L.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: Lowry is one particular painter, named here with his initials.

entries.clue: Wall Street’s direction of travel for 16 (8)

annotation.definition: Wall Street’s direction of travel for 16

blocks.note: market jargon: which way share prices are heading, where a market going neither up nor down has its own term
a cross-reference to another answer in the grid, an animal with a famously odd gait

annotation.surface: A market report on where stocks are heading.
annotation.walkthrough: 16 is CRAB, and crabs walk sideways; a market that moves neither up nor down is said to trade sideways, so Wall Street and the crab share a direction.
annotation.definitionFit: Sideways is how a crab walks and how a flat market is said to move.

entries.clue: Piece from Henri Charrière in supplement (6)

indicatorNotes.Piece from: take a piece out of the letters that follow

annotation.surface: An extract from Henri Charrière, author of Papillon, printed in a newspaper supplement.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Supplement' reads as the magazine section of a newspaper; it is the verb, to add to.
annotation.definitionFit: To enrich something is to supplement it, adding value.

entries.clue: Manual covering sex toy originally found in pieces (6)

indicatorNotes.originally: 'originally' means at the origin, so only the letter the toy starts with is used
indicatorNotes.found in: IT and T are placed inside

blocks.note: it = sex appeal, or sex itself

annotation.surface: An instruction booklet on sex toys, found in bits.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Manual' reads as a handbook; here it is the adjective, of the hand.
annotation.definitionFit: A descriptive definition: 'manual' is the adjective from Latin manus, hand, and the glove without fingers is a covering for it.

entries.clue: Root’s skied edge produces chaos (6)

indicatorNotes.skied: a skied ball goes up, and in a down clue up means reversed

blocks.note: a yam is an edible root
a hem is an edge of cloth

annotation.surface: Joe Root, the England batsman, skies an edge and causes chaos in the field.
annotation.walkthrough: Joe Root is an England cricketer, and to sky a ball is to hit it high; neither the man nor the shot survives, since root is a vegetable and skied turns it upward.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym; mayhem was once a legal term for maiming, and now means wild disorder.

entries.clue: Sedative drug offence divides American golf (6)

annotation.definitionNote: an adjective: easing, as in soothing

indicatorNotes.divides: something that divides a pair sits between them, so SIN goes between A and G

blocks.note: G = golf in the NATO alphabet

annotation.surface: A drug charge causes a rift in American golf.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sedative drug' is one phrase on the surface, but the definition stops at 'Sedative', used as an adjective.
annotation.definitionFit: A sedative remedy is an easing one: it calms and soothes.

entries.clue: Stripped briefly in front of Echo Beach (5)

indicatorNotes.briefly: cut short by the last letter
indicatorNotes.in front of: in its plain positional sense: the shortened word is placed ahead of the E

blocks.note: SHORN, stripped of wool, loses its last letter
E = echo in the NATO alphabet

annotation.surface: Getting undressed quickly ahead of a day at the beach.
annotation.walkthrough: Echo Beach is a 1980 song by Martha and the Muffins, so the two words read as one name; split, Echo is E and Beach is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A loose synonym: both name the strip of land where sea meets dry ground.

entries.clue: Buddy possibly disheartened by German army showing spirit (4,5)

blocks.note: HOLLY, as in Buddy Holly, loses its middle L
a host is an army, as in the heavenly host

annotation.surface: A friend is dispirited by a German army putting on a show of fighting spirit.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Buddy' reads as a friend; it is Buddy Holly, the 1950s rock and roll singer, and 'possibly' flags that Buddy only points to him.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: the third person of the Christian Trinity is also called the Holy Spirit.

entries.clue: Pierce Brosnan’s heartbeat (5)

blocks.note: read as heart + beat: the heart of BroSnan is its middle letter S, and a beat of a clock is a TICK

annotation.surface: The actor Pierce Brosnan's pulse.
annotation.walkthrough: Pierce Brosnan is one name on the surface; the first name is the verb to pierce, and 'heartbeat' splits into heart and beat.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: you stick a pin into a cushion, piercing it.

entries.clue: Young boy touring Northern Territory (9)

indicatorNotes.touring: the boy travels round the N

annotation.surface: A youngster on a trip round Australia's Northern Territory.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Northern Territory' names an Australian region, so the two words stick together; split, Northern is N and Territory the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: the vast Arctic island is self-governing but belongs to Denmark, so it is a territory rather than a country.
